nodes.summary: QA means quality assurance. CAPA means corrective and preventive action. HITL means human in the loop, which is the reviewer approval step.
nodes.title: Glossary

nodes.summary: There are three user roles: operator, reviewer and tenant admin. Operators can ask questions, look up lots and file requests. Reviewers approve or reject requests. Tenant admins manage users and roles
nodes.title: Access control policy

nodes.summary: The assistant answers policy, SOP and catalog questions from the approved vault and cites every claim it makes. It can look up lot status.
nodes.title: Scope of the operations assistant

nodes.summary: Audit records are kept for 7 years. Conversation turns are kept for 90 days and are then deleted. Training records are kept for 5 years, as set out in [[sop-training]].
nodes.title: Data retention policy

nodes.summary: Open deviations that reach 14 days are escalated to the Plant Manager. Deviations that reach 30 days are reported to the corporate quality board.
nodes.title: Riverside escalation policy

nodes.summary: Personal data such as email addresses, phone numbers and national ID numbers must not be entered into requests. The assistant redacts them before processing and does not store them.
nodes.title: Personal data policy

nodes.summary: Gloves and safety goggles are required in the production area at all times. Gloves are nitrile examination gloves, SKU-017, and are changed every 2 hours or after any visible contamination.
nodes.title: Personal protective equipment requirements

nodes.summary: Lot verification confirms that the protocol reference on the lot record matches the approved safety protocol PROT-SAF-7 for LOT-00044 and that the storage temperature log stays between 2 and 8 degrees
nodes.title: Safety protocol for lot verification

nodes.summary: Any spill of more than 100 millilitres must be reported to the shift supervisor within 15 minutes. The area is closed off and the spill is contained with absorbent material.
nodes.title: Spill response procedure

nodes.summary: Any change to a process, a protocol or a supplier needs a written change request. QA must review each change request within 10 business days.
nodes.title: Change control procedure

nodes.summary: Equipment must be cleaned and the cleaning verified before it changes over from one product to another. The cleaning process is validated under protocol PROT-CLN-4.
nodes.title: Cleaning validation procedure

nodes.summary: Refrigerated products such as SKU-099 must be stored between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius at all times. Storage temperature is logged every 15 minutes by the cold room monitor under protocol PROT-SAF-7.
nodes.title: Cold chain storage procedure

nodes.summary: Any deviation must be recorded within 2 business days of detection. A CAPA (corrective and preventive action) is opened for each major deviation and must be closed within 30 days.
nodes.title: Deviation and CAPA procedure

nodes.summary: At the Riverside plant every deviation must be logged within 24 hours of detection. A deviation that affects a lot is reported to the Quality Lead on the same day.
nodes.title: Riverside deviation handling

nodes.summary: A hold is placed when a lot needs more testing. The lot status becomes ON_HOLD until testing is complete.
nodes.title: Hold and reject procedure

nodes.summary: Every lot label must show the lot ID, the SKU, the expiry date and the storage range. Labels are checked by two people, and the second checker must be a different person from the first.
nodes.title: Label verification procedure

nodes.summary: Lots at the Riverside plant are released by the Quality Lead after a 48 hour stability review. Lot release requests are filed through the Riverside portal.
nodes.title: Riverside plant lot release

nodes.summary: A lot may be released only after QA review is complete and the lot status is AVAILABLE. The release decision belongs to a reviewer.
nodes.title: Lot release procedure

nodes.summary: Quarantine is used when a lot shows a possible deviation or a failed check. A quarantined lot cannot be shipped or released until a reviewer decides.
nodes.title: Quarantine procedure

nodes.summary: A recall is started when a released lot is found to be unsafe or out of specification. Customers who received the lot must be notified within 24 hours of the recall decision.
nodes.title: Recall procedure

nodes.summary: For every lot of up to 1000 units, 5 units are sampled at random. For lots of more than 1000 units, 10 units are sampled. Samples are tested under protocol PROT-TST-2.
nodes.title: Sampling and testing procedure

nodes.summary: A new supplier must pass a qualification audit under protocol PROT-SUP-3 before any of its materials are used. Qualified suppliers are re-audited every 24 months.
nodes.title: Supplier qualification procedure

nodes.summary: A temperature excursion is any reading above 8 degrees Celsius or below 2 degrees Celsius in a refrigerated store. An excursion shorter than 30 minutes is logged and the lot stays AVAILABLE.
nodes.title: Temperature excursion procedure

nodes.summary: Operators must complete the lot handling course before filing requests. Training records are kept for 5 years.
nodes.title: Operator training
